phrases.english_text: Uksudi. He used to look for snake skin and used it for medicine. He said people from long ways off came to get medicine. Still, there are a lot of snakes around there. And Granny, when I was little, I had asthma and granny made medicine for me. I wish I paid attention to what she used. “What I’m fixing here, I’m going to add cream to it. Just eat a little bit every day,” she said. When I was doing that it, it didn’t bother me and then after a long while it came back. It was good and then Ayvl(i), ...okay... he was a true believer of his using tobacco, you know. I thought, “Oh gosh.”

phrases.english_text: I used to be there cause the girl worked there. I would go home about 10 o’clock, she would drop me off and they said she started running around. And when she takes Granny with her, “Let’s take her to Vian.” “Where are we going?” I said. “To somebody named Smith,” she said. “Why do you do what he says to do?” “Let’s just go over there,” she said. So we went, and this old man was asking me. I said I didn’t believe in this stuff. I had never heard of it being medicine, I had never used tobacco and I never smoked. But this old man was asking questions and he was saying the same thing.

So, he told my aunt how I should smoke them, first the east –what's the name for ‘east?’-- smoke and blow in all [four] directions. He said, “Do not bring them in the house.” My aunt had a chicken house and that’s where she put them. I did that every day when I got up and I was sure getting tired of it after a while. At first, I just puffed a little bit and then later I went to really smoking it. And uh...boy about going on the 3rd week, I was sitting on the stump and I quit turning around.

phrases.english_text: Mike’s aunt got there and would relieve me. That girl was kinda, sorta weird because she changed right away. “What’s going on with you?” I said to her. “Nothing.” She would be crawling on the floor listening to something. She was scaring the kids. So I didn’t want to, but I started praying. They brought her kids back to her. It was Memorial Weekend they had a fight, but I don’t know what happened. Then they took their kids away again. When they called me, they said they were taking the kids and I told them let me talk to her. So when I talked to them I told her I had gone through the same thing when I was young and I said, “Don’t do that to them. Tell their aunt to bring them over here. I don’t want you to put them in a police car.” They followed her here and brought the kids. “Why did you want to do that?” I told her. “Can you tell me what it was like when you grew up?” she said to me. “To this day, I’m still scarred by it,” I told her.
